name: PubMed_search_articles
description: Search PubMed (MEDLINE), the main index of published biomedical and clinical literature, using NCBI E-utilities (esearch + esummary). Use it for published evidence on a disease, injury or procedure: clinical trials, systematic reviews, case reports and case series on diagnosis, medical or surgical treatment, operative technique, outcomes and complications, including rare conditions that guidelines do not cover; and to find articles by topic, author or journal. PubMed syntax works, e.g. 'retrocaval ureter[ti] AND laparoscopic' or 'Meckel diverticulum AND Case Reports[pt]'. Returns articles with PMID, title, authors, journal, publication year, DOI, article type, and PubMed URL (include_abstract adds abstracts). Automatically fetches rich metadata for each article. Rate limiting is automatically handled (3 req/sec without API key, 10 req/sec with key set via NCBI_API_KEY environment variable).

query.description: Search query for PubMed articles. Use keywords, author names, journal names, or MeSH terms. Examples: 'cancer immunotherapy', 'Smith J[Author]', 'Nature[Journal]', 'diabetes[MeSH]'. Use AND/OR/NOT for complex queries. Note: PubMed ANDs every space-separated keyword by default, so a long, highly specific free-text query (5+ concepts) often returns 0 results even when relevant literature exists. Prefer 2-4 key concepts, add explicit OR for synonyms, or try EuropePMC_search_articles for broader relevance-ranked full-text search if this returns 0 results.

limit.description: Number of articles to return. This sets the maximum number of articles retrieved from PubMed (max: 200).

mindate.description: Minimum date for results (format: YYYY/MM/DD or YYYY). Requires datetype to be set.

maxdate.description: Maximum date for results (format: YYYY/MM/DD or YYYY). Requires datetype to be set.

datetype.description: Type of date to filter on: 'pdat' (publication date), 'edat' (Entrez date), or 'mdat' (modification date). Required when using mindate/maxdate.

include_abstract.description: If true, best-effort fetches abstracts via efetch (adds abstract/abstract_source fields).

sort.description: Sort order for results. Valid values: 'pub_date' (newest first), 'Author' (alphabetical by first author), 'JournalName' (alphabetical by journal), 'relevance' (default PubMed ranking).

max_results.description: Alias for limit — maximum number of results to return

oneOf.description: Array of PubMed articles with metadata

authors.description: List of author names, truncated to the first 5. Check authors_truncated/author_count before citing this list — an article with exactly 5 authors and an article whose 20 authors were cut to 5 look identical here. Call PubMed_get_article with the pmid for the complete author list with affiliations.

author_count.description: Total number of authors on the article, as reported by PubMed — not the length of the truncated `authors` array.

authors_truncated.description: True when the article has more than 5 authors and `authors` therefore lists only the first 5. False means `authors` is the complete author list.

url.description: Direct URL to the article on PubMed

abstract.description: Abstract text (only when include_abstract=true and available)

pmc_url.description: PMC full text URL when PMCID is available

oneOf.description: Stub response when summaries fail (contains PMIDs and URLs only)

name: PubMed_get_article
description: Get complete metadata for a specific PubMed article by its PMID (PubMed ID) using efetch. Returns comprehensive article information including title, full abstract, complete author list with affiliations, journal details (name, volume, issue, pages), publication dates, DOI, MeSH terms, article type, grant information, and references. Essential for accessing full abstracts, detailed metadata, and citation information. Find PMIDs using PubMed_search_articles (format: integer like 12345678).

pmid.description: PubMed ID (PMID) as string or integer (e.g., '12345678' or 12345678, '33250470' or 33250470). Find PMIDs using PubMed_search_articles. Can also accept comma-separated PMIDs as string for multiple articles.

return_schema.description: Full PubMed article metadata in XML format (as string) or parsed structure

abstract.description: Abstract text, where PubMed holds one. Null for articles with no abstract, which includes most editorials and letters.

pub_date.description: Publication date as PubMed records it; the precision varies by record.

items.description: One author. The detail endpoint returns an object; the related and cited-by endpoints return a bare name string, so the element type differs by endpoint.

name.description: The author's name as PubMed records it.

author_count.description: How many authors the article has. Compare with the length of `authors` -- the list can be capped while the count is not.

doi_url.description: That DOI as a resolvable URL.

publication_types.description: All publication types PubMed assigned, e.g. ['Randomized Controlled Trial'].

mesh_terms.description: MeSH headings indexed for the article. Absent on very recent records, which are not yet indexed -- so a MeSH search misses the newest papers by construction.

name: PubMed_get_related
description: Get related PubMed articles for a specific PMID using elink. Returns a list of computationally similar articles based on title, abstract, and MeSH terms. Use this to discover additional relevant literature, find similar studies, or explore a research topic more comprehensively. The algorithm identifies articles with similar content, methodology, or subject matter. Find PMIDs using PubMed_search_articles.

pmid.description: PubMed ID (PMID) for which to find related articles (e.g., '20210808', '19879512'). Find PMIDs using PubMed_search_articles.

limit.description: Maximum number of related articles to return (default: 20, max: 100).

return_schema.description: List of related PMIDs, linkset data structure, or error message

pub_date.description: Publication date as PubMed records it; the precision varies by record.

author_count.description: How many authors the article has. Compare with the length of `authors` -- the list can be capped while the count is not.

authors_truncated.description: True when the author list was cut. The first and last author positions carry meaning in most fields, so a truncated list can lose the senior author.

doi_url.description: That DOI as a resolvable URL.

pmcid.description: PubMed Central id, where the full text is open.

pmc_url.description: The PMC page. Its presence is what says the full text can be read without a subscription.

article_type.description: What kind of article it is, e.g. 'Journal Article', 'Review'. A review and a primary report are different evidence.

relevance_score.description: How closely this article relates to the queried one. Comparable only within one result set.

name: PubMed_get_cited_by
description: Get a list of PubMed articles that cite a specific PMID using elink. Returns PMIDs of articles that have cited the input article in their reference list. Use this to track citation impact, find more recent work building on a paper, or explore how research has been applied. Essential for literature reviews, impact analysis, and staying current with research developments. Find PMIDs using PubMed_search_articles.

name: PubMed_get_links
description: Get external links (LinkOut) for a specific PubMed article by its PMID using elink. Returns URLs to full-text providers, supplementary data, related resources, clinical trials, and other external content. Use this to access full-text articles, find supplementary materials, or discover related datasets and resources. Essential for accessing paywalled content via institutional subscriptions or finding open-access versions. Find PMIDs using PubMed_search_articles.

pmid.description: PubMed ID (PMID) for which to retrieve external links (e.g., '19880848', '19822630'). Find PMIDs using PubMed_search_articles.

return_schema.description: LinkOut URLs and provider information (array of link objects or structured data)

id.description: The PubMed ID the links belong to.

objurls.description: The outbound links NCBI holds for the article -- full text, related resources, patient information.

categories.description: What kind of resource it is, e.g. ['Medical'].

attributes.description: Access attributes, e.g. ['free resource']. This is what says whether the link leads to something readable without payment.
